entries.name: Workflow automation
entries.definition: Using software to carry out the steps of a business process automatically, passing work between people and systems.

entries.name: Workflow management
entries.definition: Defining, coordinating and monitoring the steps and handoffs through which work moves through an organization.

entries.name: Workforce optimisation
entries.definition: Matching staffing levels and schedules to expected demand, as in contact centres, so that a workforce is used efficiently.

entries.name: Workforce trends
entries.definition: Understanding how the size, make-up, skills and working patterns of an organization's or an industry's workers are changing over time.

entries.name: Working with children aged 0-5
entries.definition: Caring for and teaching babies, toddlers and young children from birth to five years old.

entries.name: Worship ministry
entries.definition: The planning and leading of a church's public worship, including its music, liturgy and volunteer teams.

entries.name: Writing outlines
entries.definition: Planning a piece of writing by listing its main points and their order before drafting it.

entries.name: WSDL2Java
entries.definition: A command-line tool, found in Apache Axis and Apache CXF, that generates Java classes from a WSDL web-service description.

entries.name: wxGTK
entries.definition: The GTK port of the wxWidgets C++ toolkit, used to build cross-platform desktop applications.

entries.name: wxPerl
entries.definition: The Perl bindings for the wxWidgets GUI toolkit.

entries.name: wxPython
entries.definition: The Python bindings for the wxWidgets GUI toolkit, used to build cross-platform desktop applications.

entries.name: Wyse Management Suite
entries.definition: Dell's software for configuring, monitoring and updating Wyse thin clients and other edge devices.

entries.name: Xanthoproteic reaction
entries.definition: A chemical test in which concentrated nitric acid turns proteins that contain aromatic amino acids yellow, used to detect such proteins.

entries.name: Xbox Live Vision
entries.definition: A USB camera accessory for the Xbox 360 that adds video chat and image capture to games and Xbox Live.

entries.name: Xcalibur
entries.definition: Thermo Fisher Scientific software for controlling mass spectrometers and processing their data.

entries.name: XtraGrid
entries.definition: The DevExpress data-grid control for Windows Forms applications.

entries.name: Yahoo Messenger
entries.definition: An instant messaging service from Yahoo, shut down in 2018.

entries.name: Yahoo! Messenger protocols
entries.definition: The proprietary network protocols that Yahoo! Messenger clients used to talk to Yahoo's servers.

entries.name: YARA
entries.definition: An open-source tool that identifies and classifies malware by matching files against rules that describe text or binary patterns.

entries.name: Yardi
entries.definition: Property management and real-estate accounting software from Yardi Systems.

entries.name: Yellow Dog Linux
entries.definition: A Linux distribution for PowerPC computers, made by Terra Soft Solutions.

entries.name: Youth mentoring
entries.definition: Guiding and supporting a young person over time as an adult mentor, for example with school, work and personal choices.

entries.name: Youth ministry
entries.definition: The programmes, teaching and pastoral care a church provides for teenagers and young people.

entries.name: YunOS
entries.definition: An operating system developed by Alibaba for smartphones and other connected devices.

entries.name: z/OS
entries.definition: IBM's operating system for its z Systems mainframe computers.

entries.name: Z-Wave
entries.definition: A low-power wireless protocol that smart-home devices such as sensors, locks and switches use to communicate.

entries.name: Zemax OpticStudio
entries.definition: Software for designing and simulating optical systems such as lenses, from Zemax.

entries.name: ZENworks Asset Management
entries.definition: A ZENworks product, originally from Novell, for tracking an organization's software licences and hardware assets.

entries.name: zeroheight
entries.definition: A web platform for documenting and sharing a design system so that designers and developers work from the same guidelines.

entries.name: Zerto
entries.definition: Software for disaster recovery, backup and workload migration across virtual and cloud environments.

entries.name: Zetafax
entries.definition: Server software for sending and receiving faxes from desktops and applications across a network.

entries.name: ZFS
entries.definition: A file system and volume manager, first developed at Sun Microsystems, that combines storage pooling, snapshots and data checksums.
